title: Rotate the Matrix

concept.title: Where does a cell go?
body: To rotate a square matrix by 90 degrees **clockwise**, ask where the cell at row `i`, column `j` ends up. The first row becomes the last column, the second row the second to last column, and so on. A cell `(i, j)` moves to `(j, n - 1 - i)`.
Working out the destination formula for one cell is the whole trick. Check it with the corners: the top left cell `(0, 0)` must land at the top right `(0, n - 1)`.

statement: Rotate a square matrix of size `n` by 90 degrees clockwise and print the result.
inputFormat: The next `n` lines have `n` integers each.
outputFormat: Print the rotated matrix, `n` lines with `n` integers each.

examples.note: The first column read from the bottom, 7 4 1, becomes the first row.

hints: Find the new position of the cell in row i and column j.
The first row becomes the last column, so `(i, j)` goes to `(j, n - 1 - i)`.
Fill a second matrix with a double loop and print it.
